question: Why did West revenue fall from April 2026?
system: Don't say anything that isn't clearly supported by the data. If you are unable to answer something with the data, say so.
answer:
Based on the data provided, the West region's revenue fell from April 2026 because **D12 Carrick Stowe closed on 2026-03-27** and stopped generating revenue from the week of 2026-03-30 onward.

The data shows:
- D12 Carrick Stowe had weekly revenue ranging from €27,162 to €41,173 in its final 12 weeks of trading (average €33,687)
- From 2026-03-30 onward, D12 has dashes (no rows loaded), meaning zero revenue
- The West total dropped from an average of €133,247/week (when all three depots were trading) to €117,183/week (with only D10 and D11 trading) — a 12.1% decline

The staff notes confirm: *"2026-02-10 D12 Carrick Stowe (West), R. Pellam: Head office confirmed: Carrick Stowe closes for good on Friday 27 March. Lease not renewed"* and *"2026-03-27 D12 Carrick Stowe (West), R. Pellam: Last day of trading. All equipment off hire and returned to the central yard."*

Notably, the two remaining West depots (D10 Abermoor and D11 Lowen Quay) actually **increased** their individual revenues after D12's closure (+14.4% and +21.9% respectively), but this was not enough to offset the loss of D12's ~€33,700/week contribution.
